title: Ik heb — hebben en de ontkenning
summary: The verb hebben (to have), and today's one big thing: niet vs geen

blocks.title: The verb hebben (to have)
blocks.body: After *zijn*, this is the verb you'll reach for most. Dutch uses *hebben* where English says 'have' — and also for age and for being hungry or thirsty: *ik heb honger* (I'm hungry, literally 'I have hunger').
blocks.callout: *hij heeft* but *jij hebt* — the -eeft is only for the hij/zij/het slot.

blocks.prompt: Fill the gap: Zij ___ een kat. (She has a cat.)
blocks.explain: *zij* (she) is the hij/zij/het slot, so *heeft*. *heb* is for *ik*, *hebt* for *jij*.

blocks.prompt: Say 'I'm thirsty' in Dutch (literally: I have thirst).
blocks.explain: *Ik heb dorst.* Dutch 'has' hunger and thirst rather than 'being' them.

blocks.title: Today's one big thing: niet vs geen
blocks.body: Dutch has **two** words for 'not', and picking the right one is the whole skill. **geen** negates a noun that has no article or an *een* — 'no / not any'. **niet** negates everything else: verbs, adjectives, whole ideas. Get this contrast and your Dutch stops sounding translated.
blocks.callout: Quick test: if you could put *een* or nothing in front of the noun, use **geen**. Otherwise, **niet**.

blocks.title: geen replaces een; niet does the rest

pairs.note: *geen auto* = no car (a noun with no article). *niet* negates the verb *werk*.
*geen koffie* = not any coffee. But *de koffie* already has *de*, so its quality is negated with *niet*.

blocks.prompt: Choose: Ik heb ___ geld. (I have no money.)
blocks.explain: *geld* (money) is a bare noun with no article, so 'no money' = *geen geld*. *niet* would be wrong here.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type what you hear.
blocks.explain: *Ik heb geen honger* — I'm not hungry. Bare noun *honger*, so *geen*.

blocks.scene: Back at the café. Daan is deciding on a second round.

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Nee, dankjewel. Ik drink geen koffie meer.
lines.en: No, thanks. I'm not drinking any more coffee.

lines.speaker: Daan
lines.target: Thee dan? Ik heb geen haast, hoor.
lines.en: Tea then? I'm in no hurry, honestly.

blocks.prompt: Write two true sentences: one thing you have (*ik heb…*) and one thing you don't (*ik heb geen…* or a *niet* sentence). Then say why in English if you like.
